title: 18. Sept inventions perdues
gist: People in the past invented remarkable things, and some of these inventions are now lost: researchers are still trying to work out how they were made or how they worked. Seven examples, from the Byzantines' Greek fire and the ancient Greek Antikythera mechanism to the Inca knotted cords (quipus), a Persian weapon that shot five arrows, a luxury plant that vanished, Viking tablet weaving and the unread script of Easter Island.

body.fr: Aujourd'hui, nous avons Internet, des {{avions|planes}} et des satellites.

bd.meaning: Today we have the internet, planes and satellites.
chunks: Internet, des avions et des satellites
the internet, planes and satellites (des = some, plural)
bd.key: The little word “des”: it's the plural of un/une. English often drops it: des avions = just “planes.”

body.fr: Mais les gens {{du passé|of the past}} ont aussi inventé des choses {{incroyables|amazing}}.

bd.meaning: But people in the past also invented amazing things.
chunks: but the people of the past (du = de + le)
also invented — 'aussi' sits between the helper and the past form
amazing things — adjective after the noun
bd.key: Past = avoir + past form: ont inventé = “invented.” Little words like aussi slip in between the two parts.

body.fr: Certaines de ces inventions sont {{perdues|lost}}.

bd.meaning: Some of these inventions are lost.
bd.key: Words agree with the noun: inventions is feminine plural, so both certaines and perdues take -es.

body.fr: Les {{chercheurs|researchers}} {{essaient encore de|are still trying to}} les comprendre.

bd.meaning: Researchers are still trying to understand them.
chunks: are still trying to (essayer de + plain verb)
to understand them — 'les' (them) comes BEFORE the verb
bd.key: “them” goes before the verb: les comprendre = “understand them.” French puts le/la/les in front of the verb, not after.

body.fr: {{Voici|here are}} sept exemples.

bd.meaning: Here are seven examples.
chunks: here is / here are — one fixed word
bd.key: “voici” = “here is / here are.” It never changes, singular or plural.

body.fr: Les Byzantins ont inventé le {{feu grégeois|Greek fire}} au {{septième siècle|seventh century}}.

bd.meaning: The Byzantines invented Greek fire in the seventh century.
chunks: Greek fire — the set French name; 'grégeois' is an old word for 'Greek'
in the seventh century (au = à + le)
bd.key: Centuries use “au”: au septième siècle = “in the seventh century.” -ième turns a number into “-th.”

body.fr: C'est une {{arme|weapon}} {{terrible|fearsome}} contre les bateaux {{ennemis|enemy}}.

bd.meaning: It's a fearsome weapon against enemy ships.
chunks: a fearsome weapon — 'terrible' often means 'fearsome', not just 'very bad'
against enemy ships — 'ennemis' after the noun
bd.key: Adjective after the noun: les bateaux ennemis = “the enemy ships,” word order flipped from English.

body.fr: {{Selon la légende|according to legend}}, ce feu {{brûle|burns}} même sur l'eau.

bd.meaning: According to legend, this fire burns even on water.
chunks: this fire (ce = this, before a masculine noun)
bd.key: “selon” = “according to.” A handy word in news: selon la légende, selon les chercheurs.

body.fr: Les Byzantins l'ont utilisé {{pendant|for (a length of time)}} plus de 500 ans.

bd.meaning: The Byzantines used it for more than 500 years.
chunks: used it — l' (= le, 'it') sits before the helper 'ont'
bd.key: “it” before the helper: in the past, le goes in front of ont: l'ont utilisé = “used it.”

body.fr: Mais aujourd'hui, {{personne ne connaît|nobody knows}} la {{recette|recipe}}.

bd.meaning: But today nobody knows the recipe.
bd.key: “personne ne …” = “nobody …”: personne takes the place of pas in the sandwich. Don't add pas as well.

body.fr: {{Il y avait|there was}} peut-être du {{pétrole|oil (petroleum)}} {{dedans|in it}}.

bd.meaning: There may have been oil in it.
chunks: there was / there were — the past of 'il y a'
bd.key: il y a → il y avait: “there is” becomes “there was.” Same set phrase, only the middle changes.

body.fr: En 1901, des {{plongeurs|divers}} ont trouvé un objet {{au fond de la mer|at the bottom of the sea}}, près d'une île grecque.

bd.meaning: In 1901, divers found an object at the bottom of the sea, near a Greek island.
chunks: un objet au fond de la mer
an object at the bottom of the sea
near a Greek island — 'grecque' is the feminine of 'grec'
bd.key: “en” + year: en 1901 = “in 1901.” Years take en; centuries take au.

body.fr: C'est le {{mécanisme d'Anticythère|the Antikythera mechanism}}.

bd.meaning: It's the Antikythera mechanism.
chunks: of Antikythera — the island's French spelling
bd.key: Place names change spelling in French: Antikythera becomes Anticythère, just as London becomes Londres.

body.fr: Il a plus de 2 000 ans et il a des {{dizaines|dozens}} de {{roues dentées|gears}} en bronze.

bd.meaning: It is more than 2,000 years old and it has dozens of bronze gears.
chunks: it is more than 2,000 years old — literally 'it has' the years
bronze gears — literally 'toothed wheels in bronze'
bd.key: Age uses “avoir”: French says a thing has its years: il a 2 000 ans = “it is 2,000 years old.”

body.fr: Selon les chercheurs, il {{peut prédire|can predict}} les {{mouvements|movements}} de la lune et les {{éclipses de soleil|solar eclipses}}.

bd.meaning: According to researchers, it can predict the movements of the moon and solar eclipses.
chunks: and solar eclipses — literally 'eclipses of sun'
bd.key: Helper + plain verb: peut prédire = “can predict.” Only peut changes.

body.fr: Pour les experts, c'est le {{plus vieil|oldest}} {{ordinateur|computer}} du monde.

bd.meaning: Experts say it is the oldest computer in the world.
chunks: for the experts / in the experts' view
the oldest computer (le plus + adjective = the most …)
in the world — French says 'of the world'
bd.key: “vieux” becomes “vieil” before a vowel: vieil ordinateur, so the words flow. It also sits before the noun, like vrai and grand.

body.fr: En Amérique du Sud, il y a les {{quipus|quipus (knotted cords)}} : des {{cordes|cords}} avec beaucoup de petits {{nœuds|knots}}.

bd.meaning: In South America there are quipus: cords with lots of little knots.
chunks: in South America (en before a continent)
with lots of little knots — 'beaucoup de', never 'beaucoup des'
bd.key: “beaucoup de” stays “de”: beaucoup de nœuds, not des. Same as beaucoup de gens.

body.fr: Des {{peuples|peoples}} anciens, comme les Incas, ont utilisé ces cordes pour {{noter|record, write down}} des informations.

bd.meaning: Ancient peoples, like the Incas, used these cords to record information.
chunks: to record information — 'informations' is plural in French
bd.key: pour + plain verb = “in order to”: pour noter = “to record.” The verb after pour stays plain.

body.fr: Mais les chercheurs {{ne savent pas encore|don't yet know how to}} lire les plus vieux quipus.

bd.meaning: But researchers can't yet read the oldest quipus.
chunks: don't yet know (how to) — the ne…pas sandwich plus 'encore' (yet)
bd.key: “savoir” + plain verb = “know how to”: ils ne savent pas lire = “they can't read (don't know how).”

body.fr: Le {{panjagan|panjagan}} est une arme {{perse|Persian}} très ancienne.

bd.meaning: The panjagan is a very old Persian weapon.
bd.key: “arme” is feminine, so ancien becomes ancienne, even though the panjagan itself is le.

body.fr: Selon des textes anciens, avec cette arme, les soldats {{tirent|shoot}} cinq {{flèches|arrows}} {{en même temps|at the same time}}.

bd.meaning: According to old texts, with this weapon soldiers shoot five arrows at once.
chunks: the soldiers shoot (tirer = to shoot / to pull)
five arrows at the same time
bd.key: “en même temps” = “at the same time.” A ready-made phrase worth keeping whole.

body.fr: Le mot {{vient de|comes from}} « panj », qui {{veut dire|means}} « cinq » en persan.

bd.meaning: The word comes from “panj,” which means “five” in Persian.
chunks: the word comes from 'panj' (venir de = come from)
which means — literally 'which wants to say'
bd.key: “vouloir dire” = “to mean.” Ça veut dire… = “that means…” — very common in speech.

body.fr: Mais {{on ne sait pas|we don't know}} comment il {{marche|works}}.

bd.meaning: But nobody knows how it works.
chunks: we / people don't know (on = people in general)
how it works — 'marcher' = to walk, but also 'to work' for machines
bd.key: “on” = people / we in general: on ne sait pas = “nobody knows / we don't know.”

body.fr: Un historien pense que c'est peut-être une {{sorte de|kind of}} {{arbalète|crossbow}}.

bd.meaning: One historian thinks it may be a kind of crossbow.
chunks: it is maybe / it may be
a kind of crossbow (de → d' before a vowel)
bd.key: “penser que” = “to think that”: French keeps the que; English can drop “that.”

body.fr: Le {{silphium|silphium}} est une {{plante|plant}} {{sauvage|wild}} d'Afrique du Nord.

bd.meaning: Silphium is a wild plant from North Africa.
chunks: is a wild plant — adjective after the noun
bd.key: Adjective after the noun: une plante sauvage = “a wild plant.”

body.fr: Les Grecs et les Romains la {{mangent|eat}} et l'utilisent comme {{médicament|medicine}}.

bd.meaning: The Greeks and Romans eat it and use it as medicine.
chunks: eat it (la = it, for the feminine 'plante')
and use it (la → l' before a vowel)
bd.key: “la” = “it” for a feminine thing, and it goes before the verb: la mangent = “eat it.”

body.fr: Elle coûte très cher : son {{poids|weight}} en {{argent|silver}} !

bd.meaning: It's very expensive: its weight in silver!
chunks: it costs a lot (elle = the plant)
bd.key: “argent” = silver AND money. Context tells you which; here it's the metal.

body.fr: Mais au premier siècle, la plante {{disparaît|disappears}}.

bd.meaning: But in the first century, the plant disappears.
chunks: but in the first century (premier = first)
bd.key: Present for history: French news often tells past events in the present to make them vivid. Here disparaît = “disappeared.”

body.fr: Pourquoi ? Les chercheurs {{ne sont pas d'accord|don't agree}}.

bd.meaning: Why? Researchers don't agree.
chunks: why? (note the space before ? in French)
don't agree — literally 'are not in agreement'
bd.key: “être d'accord” = “to agree”: French uses être, not a verb “to agree.” D'accord ! alone = “OK!”

body.fr: À l'{{époque|time, era}} des Vikings, on {{tisse|weaves}} de belles {{bandes de tissu|strips of cloth}} avec des {{tablettes|tablets (small flat cards)}}.

bd.meaning: In Viking times, people weave beautiful strips of cloth using tablets.
chunks: in the time of the Vikings
beautiful strips of cloth — 'des' becomes 'de' before 'belles'
bd.key: “des” → “de” before an adjective: des bandes but de belles bandes. In casual speech you'll also hear des belles.

body.fr: Certains {{motifs|patterns, designs}} sont très {{compliqués|complicated}}.

bd.meaning: Some patterns are very complicated.
chunks: some patterns (masculine plural: certains, not certaines)
bd.key: Words agree with the noun: motifs is masculine plural, so certains and compliqués take -s, not -es.

body.fr: Une {{historienne|historian (female)}} les {{étudie depuis|has been studying for}} des dizaines d'années.

bd.meaning: One historian has been studying them for decades.
chunks: a (female) historian — the -ne ending marks a woman
studies them (les = the patterns, before the verb)
for decades — literally 'since tens of years'
bd.key: depuis + present = “has been … for”: elle les étudie depuis… = “she has been studying them for…” French uses the present because it's still going on.

body.fr: Mais pour beaucoup de motifs, personne ne sait encore comment les {{refaire|remake, make again}}.

bd.meaning: But for many patterns, nobody yet knows how to make them again.
chunks: how to make them again (re- = again, like English)
bd.key: “re-” = “again”: faire → refaire, just like make → remake.

body.fr: Sur l'{{île de Pâques|Easter Island}}, il y a 27 vieilles {{tablettes en bois|wooden tablets}} avec des {{symboles|symbols}}.

bd.meaning: On Easter Island there are 27 old wooden tablets with symbols.
chunks: there are 27 old (vieilles = feminine plural of vieux)
wooden tablets — 'en bois' = made of wood
bd.key: “en” + material = “made of”: en bois = wooden, en bronze = bronze.

body.fr: Cette {{écriture|script, writing}} {{s'appelle|is called}} le rongorongo.

bd.meaning: This script is called rongorongo.
bd.key: “s'appeler” = “to be called”: the same verb as je m'appelle… (“my name is…”).

body.fr: Personne ne sait encore la lire.

bd.meaning: Nobody can read it yet.
chunks: to read it (la = the script, before the verb)
bd.key: “personne ne …” again: personne replaces pas. Nobody has cracked it.

body.fr: Est-ce une vraie {{langue écrite|written language}} ? On ne sait pas.

bd.meaning: Is it a real written language? We don't know.
chunks: is it — question by swapping 'c'est' around
a real written language ('vraie' before, 'écrite' after the noun)
bd.key: Question by flipping: c'est → est-ce ? = “is it?” One of the three ways to ask a question.

body.fr: Une chercheuse en Italie fait des {{modèles en 3D|3D models}} de presque toutes ces tablettes.

bd.meaning: A researcher in Italy is making 3D models of almost all these tablets.
chunks: a (female) researcher in Italy (en + feminine country)
bd.key: “-eur” → “-euse” for a woman: chercheur → chercheuse.

body.fr: Selon elle, si c'est une vraie écriture, on {{va bientôt la lire|is soon going to read it}}.

bd.meaning: In her view, if it is a real script, people will soon be able to read it.
chunks: soon read it ('la' still sits right before 'lire')
bd.key: Future = aller + plain verb: on va lire = “we're going to read.” Small words like bientôt and la squeeze in between.

grammar.en: personne ne … = nobody. It's the ne … pas sandwich with personne in place of pas. It turns up three times here: personne ne connaît, and twice personne ne sait encore.
le / la / les = it / them, BEFORE the verb. la mangent = “eat it,” les comprendre = “understand them,” l'ont utilisé = “used it.” In the past, they sit before the helper.

grammar.fr: Elle les étudie depuis des dizaines d'années
grammar.en: depuis + present = “has been … for.” French uses the present for something that started in the past and is still going on.

quiz.q: Combien de flèches le panjagan tire-t-il en même temps ?
quiz.a: Cinq — « panj » veut dire « cinq » en persan. (Five — “panj” means “five” in Persian.)

flag: Big compression: the long New York Times piece (9 Nov 2026) is cut to a few lines per invention, and I dropped the intro examples, most names and quotes, and side details (Caesar's silphium stock, the Wari before the Incas, the Viking band replication). Several past events are told in the present (la plante disparaît, les soldats tirent, il peut prédire) to keep tenses simple; a native would usually say il pouvait, tiraient, etc. feu grégeois and mécanisme d'Anticythère are the standard French names. The article says “oldest known computer”; I dropped “known.” Bandes de tissu is my plain wording; a textile specialist would say galons or tissage aux tablettes. The source doesn't give the researcher in Italy's nationality, so I wrote en Italie (she is at the University of Bologna).
